# Separately deprotect the PTC patches, then restore the native backbone

## Decision

The strongest refinement is to replace the proposed 80-nt patch at positions 2437–2516 with a **52-nt D/Ψ patch and a 28-nt dense mixed patch**, join them covalently, and retain the ordinary magnesium/temperature reconstitution baseline. This localizes the critical chemistry experiment and avoids exposing D to the ho5C synthesis/deprotection workflow. It does **not** establish that the dense four-modification patch has already been made.

I do not presently claim that a ligation splint can select the productive ribosome assembly path. An aligned, ligatable nick is a local chemical condition. A misfolded RNA can satisfy that condition, and a globally productive fold can hide its nick. Removing the splint also removes its imposed geometry. Neither the DALI results nor the modified-nucleotide extension results demonstrate global fold discrimination, reusable resetting of a chemically intact 23S ribosome, full translation fidelity, or working lifetime.

## Exact practical refinement

Positions refer to the 2,904-nt ENA V00331.1 reference already checked against 4YBB entity 22. G2445 remains unmodified during chemical manufacture and is later methylated by RlmKL.

| Patch | Positions | Length | Marks |
|---|---|---:|---|
| DP52 | 2437–2488 | 52 nt | D2449, Ψ2457 |
| DENSE28 | 2489–2516 | 28 nt | Cm2498, ho5C2501, m2A2503, Ψ2504 |

The modification-annotated sequences are:

```text
DP52
GUACUCCGGGGA[D]AACAGGC[Psi]GAUACCGCCCAAGAGUUCAUAUCGACGGCGG

DENSE28
UGUUUGGCA[Cm]CU[ho5C]G[m2A][Psi]GUCGGCUCAUCA
```

The new bond is after G2488, before U2489. Both nick termini are canonical ribonucleotides with the usual 3′-OH/5′-phosphate chemistry. Cm2498 is inside the right 12-nt splint flank, so the original calculation for modification-free local duplexes cannot be copied to this junction. Full-length product purification and chemical qualification remain necessary.

### What chemistry precedent actually supports

Gasparutto et al. chemically synthesized a natural *E. coli* alanine tRNA containing D, ribothymidine and Ψ and measured alanine acceptance. This earns coexistence of D and Ψ in one chemically synthesized RNA under a compatible protection scheme; it is not evidence that this exact 52-mer has the same recovery. [Gasparutto1992]

CATALYTIC COMPLETION AS AN ASSEMBLY EXIT: PROOFS AND FAILURES
2026-11-01. Original construction and analysis in this investigation.
Status: mathematical and molecular construction; no new wet-lab result.

Purpose: recover a working physical RNA-protein machine while retaining the
chemistry of the RNA that was manufactured. Recovering its DNA sequence is a
different operation. Reverse transcription/transcription do not reproduce a
complete modification pattern or assembled state.

No variable below is assigned a favorable experimental value for the new
realization. Rates from short peptides, isolated domains, other organisms or
other immobilization geometries are not substituted.

1. LOAD PATH: WHY COLLECTION IS NOT AN EXACT CATALYTIC CERTIFICATE

A ribosome is halted at a stop codon without class-I release factors. Capture
its nascent product through a distal affinity handle outside the exit tunnel.
The connection is support--handle--peptide--ester--tRNA--ribosome, with further
noncovalent peptide/tunnel contacts. The intended event is cognate-RF-promoted
ester hydrolysis, followed by physical exit of the same manufactured subunits.

Proposition 1. Collection certifies a chosen catalytic event exactly only if
every accessible path to collection crosses that event, and the collected
object is the candidate that traversed the path.

Proof. A noncertifying path with nonzero probability is a counterexample.
A passenger is also a counterexample. Conversely the two conditions force
the identified collected object's trajectory through the event.

This physical design DOES NOT satisfy an exact cut condition. Peptidyl-tRNA
can dissociate intact; the affinity attachment can dissociate; hydrolysis can
occur without correct stop recognition. Multiple ribosomes can share a
message. completion_exit.py explicitly enumerates these bypasses.

The original simultaneous termination/recycling version adds an avoidable
bypass: RF3/RRF/EF-G can promote peptidyl-tRNA drop-off. It is rejected.
The corrected version collects a class-I-RF-only eluate FIRST and recycles it
in a separate vessel. Sufficient RF1 for a single-turnover pulse is charged;
efficient RF1 cycling on the support is not assumed. This removes one
reagent-enabled bypass, not intrinsic leakage.
